explanation: Retrospective detector of conventional multi-word designations and specifications: the pole fires on the tokens of a titled office or affiliation chain ('She is an assistant professor of medical oncology at a teaching hospital' 7.7 on ' at'), of an institution or place name ('He works at the University of Pittsburgh Graduate School of Public Health' 5.6 on ' Graduate'; 'the Project on Emerging Nanotechnologies at the Wilson Center' 3.5 on ' Wilson'), of a recipe/measurement line or fixed culinary pairing ('- 1 cup sliced mushrooms' 6-11 on ' cup'; 'Add some garlic and oregano to the pan' 5.4 on ' and'), or of the first piece of a word the tokenizer splits at a rare boundary (' wed' in wedlock 4.5, ' des' in deserts 4.7, ' tid' in tideline up to 9.9), peaking on whichever token opens the next slot (' of', ' at', ' the', ' and', ' or', ' per', a list comma) or fills it. It is near zero on the same words, and on ordinary content nouns, in plain single-clause prose ('a doctor who treats cancer patients at a large hospital' 1.4 for the same ' at'; 'a famous professor of medicine at a hospital' 0.3; 'We visited New York City and Boston Harbor' 0.5; capitalization alone, 'ROOM 402 in the MAIN BUILDING', 0.2), and its output direction is nearly orthogonal to the vocabulary (Jacobian-lens list incoherent, kurtosis 3.3; zero-ablating the pole at its own peaks gives KL ~2e-3 with no coherent token lost), so it reads out such material rather than preparing a specific upcoming token.
